skill.name: ai-image-generation
skill.description: Generate and edit AI images through the inference.sh belt CLI using GPT-Image-2, FLUX, Gemini, Grok, Seedream, Reve, and related models.
skill.summary: Run remote image generation, editing, upscaling, and stitching tasks from supported AI assistants.
skill.author: skills-shell

security_audit.summary: The skill is legitimate image-generation guidance, but it intentionally executes belt and npx CLI commands. Those commands call remote inference services and may send prompts, image URLs, and generated assets outside the local environment. I found no prompt-injection text or hidden data-exfiltration instructions.

remediation.suggestion: Pin trusted install sources or versions for belt-related skill installation examples.
Add a privacy note explaining that prompts, image URLs, and outputs are sent to inference.sh and model providers.
Tell users to avoid private images unless they accept the provider data handling terms.

content.value_statement: Creating consistent AI image outputs across many providers can require complex CLI knowledge. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical prompts for inference.sh image workflows.
actual_capabilities: Runs text-to-image examples for GPT-Image-2, FLUX, Gemini, Grok, Seedream, Reve, and related apps.
Shows image editing and inpainting patterns using input image URLs.
Includes app discovery commands for image models in the belt app store.
Provides upscaling and image stitching examples for existing image URLs.
Lists related skills for focused image, video, avatar, and background removal workflows.
Documents the required belt login and inference.sh CLI setup path.
limitations: Requires the external inference.sh belt CLI and an authenticated account.
Sends prompts and image references to remote model providers.
Does not include local model execution or offline image generation.
Image quality, pricing, and model availability depend on external services.

use_cases.title: Create Product Mockups
use_cases.description: Generate product scenes, studio shots, and campaign variants for review before production design work.

use_cases.title: Produce Marketing Visuals
use_cases.description: Create social media concepts, posters, and branded illustration drafts from natural language prompts.

use_cases.title: Prototype Visual Workflows
use_cases.description: Test image generation, editing, upscaling, and stitching flows through one CLI-driven assistant workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Simple Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the AI image generation skill to create a square image of [subject] in [style]. Choose a suitable model and explain the result location.

prompt_templates.title: Edit an Existing Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to edit this image URL: [image URL]. Change [specific element] while preserving [important details]. Tell me what provider receives the image.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Model Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the available image models for [goal]. Recommend one model for quality, one for speed, and one for cost before running anything.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Batch Creative Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a workflow for [campaign or project]. Include generation, editing, upscaling, review points, cost controls, and privacy checks before execution.

output_examples.input: User asks for a product photo of sneakers with studio lighting.
output_examples.output: The assistant selects GPT-Image-2 or FLUX, runs a suitable image app, and returns the generated image link or file details.

output_examples.input: User provides an image URL and requests a sunset beach background.
output_examples.output: The assistant uses an image editing app and explains that the source image is sent to the remote provider.

output_examples.input: User asks to upscale a finished concept image.
output_examples.output: The assistant uses an upscaling app, reports the output location, and reminds the user to review quality before publishing.

best_practices: Use non-sensitive images unless the provider privacy policy permits your content.
State desired aspect ratio, style, text, and quality before generation.
Review model pricing and availability before running many generations.
anti_patterns: Sending private client images without approval.
Requesting many model runs without a cost limit.
Using vague prompts when exact product details or text rendering are required.

faq.question: Does this run images locally?
faq.answer: No. The skill uses inference.sh and remote model providers through the belt CLI.

faq.question: Can Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. Claude Code can use it when belt is available and authentication is configured.

faq.question: Can Codex use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. Codex can follow the documented workflow in environments that allow the belt command.

faq.question: Which models does it mention?
faq.answer: It mentions GPT-Image-2, FLUX, Gemini, Grok, Seedream, Reve, ImagineArt, P-Image, and Topaz upscaling.

faq.question: Can it edit existing images?
faq.answer: Yes. Several examples use image URLs for editing, inpainting, upscaling, and stitching.

faq.question: Is it safe for sensitive images?
faq.answer: Use caution. Prompts and image URLs may be sent to remote services outside your workspace.
